solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Game old soldiers fought at the front

indicators.note: the verb for fought is placed at the front, ahead of the old and soldiers pieces

parts.note: fought means battled
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers

explanation.surface: Veteran troops fought out some contest on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTLEDORE is an old game, the forerunner of badminton, played with a racket and shuttlecock.
explanation.definitionFit: Battledore was an early shuttlecock pastime, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Shine where gymnastic skill is required

definitions.meaning: to shine is to ..., as a face ... with joy
the balance ... is a gymnastics apparatus

explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for radiating light or happiness and the narrow apparatus gymnasts balance on.

clue.text: Rubbish put out by 23

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters of the referenced entry are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 23 down is HOST

explanation.surface: Garbage set out by a neighbour at number 23.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' refers to the solution of 23 down, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is informal British slang for nonsense or rubbish talk.

clue.text: Minor skin problem? You don't need b____ surgeon!

indicators.note: the clue says to do without the letter b, so it is taken away

parts.note: a blister is a minor skin problem
the letter b itself

explanation.surface: A small skin complaint needs no surgeon, the clue jokes with a mock censored word.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister was the pioneering British surgeon of antiseptic surgery; the blanked 'b____' mimics a softened swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lister, the Victorian pioneer of antiseptics, was a famous surgeon.

clue.text: A Maoist doctrine could make this very tricky!

definitions.text: A Maoist doctrine could make this very tricky!

indicators.note: could make says these words can be rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: Bringing in rule by the people would be hard under Maoist doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of 'A Maoist doctrine' rearrange to the answer; the whole clue also says a Maoist creed would make it hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Democratisation means spreading power to the people, something hard to achieve under Maoist rule.

clue.text: Soldier expressing bitterness audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: rancour means bitterness

explanation.surface: A trooper voicing his resentment out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranker is a soldier in the ranks, or an officer who rose from them.

clue.text: Resistance units on a royal mission

definitions.meaning: the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance
... abbreviates On Her Majesty's Service, printed on British official mail

explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the electrical resistance unit, and the initials of On Her Majesty's Service.

clue.text: The woman wearies when keeping four cows?

parts.note: her stands for the woman

indicators.note: the wearying word keeps another piece inside it

parts.note: bores means wearies
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: She grows tired of looking after four cows.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that cows are only an example of plant-eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows eat grass, so they are examples of plant-eating animals.

clue.text: Team of senior citizens getting beef?

parts.note: silver, as in the silver-haired, describes senior citizens
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A pensioners' team gets angry about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting beef' reads as having a grievance; silverside is a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a cut of beef from the outer thigh, so an example of it.

clue.text: Reckoning as fools fellows in street

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: the fellows go inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: men are fellows

explanation.surface: Judging some fools and men out on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation or estimate, a synonym of a reckoning.

clue.text: River in the country beginning to disappear

indicators.note: the first letter of the country word is to go

parts.note: rural means in the country

explanation.surface: A rural river is starting to vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural is a river flowing from Russia through Kazakhstan.

clue.text: Article falsely acclaimed as scholarly

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: falsely means the letters are set out wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of writing undeservedly praised as learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Academical is an older synonym for academic, meaning scholarly.

clue.text: Do what someone else has done and support clubs?

definitions.text: Do what someone else has done

definitions.meaning: in card games, playing a club when clubs are led

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means imitating others, and literally playing a card of the suit led, such as clubs.

clue.text: A revolutionary having a rest it seems, lying on the shore

indicators.note: the revolutionary is having a rest, i.e. is in bed, so goes inside it

parts.note: bed is where one rests
Che Guevara is the classic crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel is taking a break, stretched out on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A beached boat or whale is stranded on the shore.

clue.text: Be antagonistic almost when you see rodents

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: averse means opposed or antagonistic

explanation.surface: Feeling hostile at the sight of rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: Beavers are large semi-aquatic rodents.

clue.text: Theologian holding point of view was a swinger

indicators.note: holding means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian
an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: A divine with opinions turned out to be a swinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' suggests a hip partygoer; here it is just something that dangles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dangled hung loosely and swung to and fro.

clue.text: Plant could provide something spicy, right?

parts.note: a clove is a spice

explanation.surface: Asking whether a plant might yield a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low-growing plant of the pea family.

clue.text: Wild party outside home brings depression

indicators.note: the party goes outside the home word

parts.note: a rave is a wild party
in means at home

explanation.surface: A loud party outside the house leaves someone low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low spirits; here it is a dip in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A ravine is a deep narrow gorge, a depression in the ground.

clue.text: Many a lorry driver will perform up to expectations

definitions.meaning: a lorry driver literally delivers goods
the idiom for doing what was promised

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the haulier's job, and idiomatically meeting what was promised or expected.

clue.text: What I'll give you in all sincerity? Gosh!

definitions.text: What I'll give you in all sincerity?
definitions.meaning: a promise given sincerely is one's word

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, a sincere promise; as an idiom, an exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Young woman given work is a bit lumpy

parts.note: doll is slang for a young woman
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A girl given a job finds it a little lumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as an adjective but means a lumpy bit, a shapeless mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless lump of soft food, a lumpy bit.

clue.text: Hero was first to gather information

indicators.note: to gather means the first piece collects the second within it

parts.note: led means was first or in front
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A champion took the lead in collecting intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a celebrated figure, a famous hero.

clue.text: A measure of class

definitions.meaning: an old measure of distance, about three miles
in a different ... means in a different class

explanation.definitionFit: An old unit of distance and a level of quality, as in not in the same league.

clue.text: Comforted in such a manner having got thrashed

parts.note: so means in such a manner
laced is an old word for thrashed or beaten

explanation.surface: Someone consoled in this way after a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Solaced means given solace, synonym of comforted.

clue.text: Fish must be caught — focus of activity

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hub is a centre of activity

explanation.surface: A fish has to be landed at the centre of the action.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Entertainer of a multitude

definitions.meaning: a ... is a great number, as in a ... of angels

explanation.definitionFit: One who receives guests, and a large crowd or throng.

clue.text: Sun is one name for tabloid

definitions.meaning: the sun is an example of a heavenly body that shines
the Daily ... is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: Our sun is an example of the celestial body; also a British tabloid newspaper title.

clue.text: Spooner's purchasing milk cart as form of transport

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: buying means purchasing
a milk float is the British electric milk delivery cart

explanation.surface: Someone buying a milk delivery vehicle to get around.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk float is a small British electric van delivering milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaplane whose fuselage floats is a mode of transport.

clue.text: Departed from school at Easter

indicators.note: from tells us the letters come out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone left school at Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: The late means the dead, so departed in the sense of deceased.

clue.text: Old writer, maybe I will offer communication for wide readership

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
a landlord who lets rooms is a letter, someone offering them

explanation.surface: An elderly author might offer a message to many readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' here means one who lets property, a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A public letter, published in a newspaper, is meant for wide readership.
